content:
The test image shows a young soybean plant that has collapsed/damped off at or near the soil line. Key observations:
- Severe wilting with dead/brown leaves
- Damage concentrated at the hypocotyl/soil line area
- Stem appears constricted/lesioned near the soil
- Sandy/dry soil conditions

Top candidates: Rhizoctonia (sunken firm lesions at soil line), Pythium_damping_off (soft rot), Phytophthora (dark brown stem lesion).

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Young soybean seedling that has completely wilted/collapsed at the soil line
- Damage concentrated at the hypocotyl/stem base
- Dry, sandy soil conditions (not wet/saturated)
- Dead, brown leaves; stem bent/fallen

**Comparison with references:**
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reddish-brown, sunken, firm and DRY lesions at the soil line — matches perfectly with the dry sandy conditions and hypocotyl-level collapse seen in the test image
- **Pythium**: Water-soaked soft rot in very early seedlings — doesn't match (Pythium reference showed much younger seedlings/seed rot stage, and requires wet conditions)
- **Phytophthora**: Dark brown lesion extending up from taproot, typically in wet/saturated soils — doesn't match the dry soil conditions
- **Charcoal_Rot/SDS**: More mature plant diseases — don't match this seedling-stage collapse
- **Anthracnose**: Late-season disease with black fungal bodies on mature pods/stems — doesn't match

The dry soil conditions, seedling-stage collapse, and damage focused at the hypocotyl/soil line strongly point to Rhizoctonia.
